title: The Lighthouse Keepers Who Vanished
notes: Register: cool. Lay out the evidence and resist the supernatural reading. The reveal in Part 4 is that the famous version is fiction; never smug.
No photographs of the three keepers are used. None on Commons are clearly licensed, and a widely circulated group photograph's provenance is uncertain. Do not add one.

The keepers appear as vague-faced cartoon figures only in their routine work (s13-s15). In the reconstruction of what happened (s40-s42, s56) they are tokens on a plan, never drawn. The wave is never drawn at all, not even as a line on a diagram: it is carried by the real cliff photographs held still.
The relief boat Hesperus is not drawn either; it appears only as a small token on the map.
The 1903 Admiralty chart (p03) is public domain and a genuine near-contemporary document. It is the only primary-source image in the video and the only high-resolution one.
The quoted 'log entries' (s48-s49) are set as type with a source? tag. They are never shown as handwriting in a logbook, and no generated image presents a real magazine title or cover.
LOW RESOLUTION, SYSTEMIC: every landscape photograph is from geograph.org.uk at roughly 640px wide. They are prints laid out on the evidence desk, at native size, never stretched.
Every landscape photograph is by Chris Downer, Peter Standing, Marc Calhoun or JJM under CC BY-SA 2.0. All require attribution.
Every archival URL was resolved from the Commons API.
Guide object: McArthur's oilskin on its hook (s03, returns s37-s39). Bookend: the clean, full, unlit lamp.
